children: Wall Street's major averages were higher on Monday as technology stocks rose ahead of several Magnificent Seven tech stocks' earnings reports and the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday.
Now, here are four news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:
Anthropic files landmark S-1 for Nasdaq listing:

its S-1 prospectus with the SEC on Monday, moving closer to an initial public offering during a volatile period for AI-related stocks. The company will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as lead underwriters. The IPO is expected during the week of November 16 and could raise approximately $100 billion, reaching a valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. Anthropic reported first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion, a 1,258% increase from $1.1 billion during the same period in 2025, while its operating margin improved from negative 221% in Q1 2025 to positive 19% in Q2 2026.
EQT to acquire Range Resources in $12.8B deal:
15.3% in pre-market trading after EQT Corp.

agreed to acquire the company in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $12.83 billion, creating the largest U.S. natural gas producer with more than 9 Bcfe/day of output and control of nearly 3 million net acres in the Appalachian Basin. EQT will issue 0.987 shares for each Range share, representing a 21% premium to Friday's closing price of $45.52. The combined company would have a pro forma enterprise value exceeding $50 billion, with EQT shareholders owning approximately 73% and Range investors holding the remaining 27%.
Oil prices drop as Middle East talks loom:

Crude oil futures  declined following news that Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman will meet with Iran's president and National Security Council chief in Tehran to de-escalate regional tensions. Front-month Nymex crude for December delivery fell 1.4% to $101.80 per barrel, while front-month Brent December crude edged 0.7% lower to $115.88 per barrel. Prices dropped despite continued attacks over the weekend, with Iran-backed Houthis claiming strikes on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pipeline and Riyadh's main airport.
Verizon beats Q3 estimates and raises full-year guidance:

reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.31 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.27, while revenue rose 1.5% year over year to $34.31 billion. The telecom giant added 406,000 postpaid phone subscribers, its strongest third-quarter performance in five years, and 137,000 postpaid net accounts, its best quarterly result in more than a decade. The company raised its full-year adjusted EPS forecast to $5.05 at the midpoint and increased its postpaid phone net additions target to 1.15 million from 875,000 previously.
